title: Beyond the 956: Dan Hicks, longtime voice of NBC Sports, dies at 64
excerpt: Dan Hicks, the longtime voice of NBC Sports golf and Olympic swimming, died November 11, 2026, at 64, following an acute illness. His wife, broadcaster Hannah Storm, and NBC Sports announced the death.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Dan Hicks, the longtime voice of NBC Sports and the soundtrack of golf and Olympic swimming for a generation of American viewers, has died at 64.

Hicks died Wednesday, November 11, 2026, in Connecticut, following an acute illness. His wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, announced the death Thursday, writing, “Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness. He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.” NBC Sports, USA Today, the PGA Tour and the USGA confirmed the death. No further details about the illness have been disclosed.

Born June 2, 1962, in Tucson, Arizona, Hicks began his broadcasting career at CNN in 1989 before joining NBC Sports in 1992. He became the network’s lead golf play-by-play announcer in 2000, a role he held for more than 25 years, calling U.S. Opens, Ryder Cups, Presidents Cups and The Players Championship, and narrating some of the biggest moments of the Tiger Woods era.

Hicks was also the voice of Olympic swimming at a record eight Summer Games, teaming with Rowdy Gaines since Atlanta in 1996, and called Alpine skiing at the Winter Games. He covered the NFL and NBA for NBC and returned as the lead play-by-play voice of Notre Dame football in 2024. He was scheduled to call this weekend’s Notre Dame–Boston College game. He won a Sports Emmy as part of NBC’s coverage of the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Hicks is survived by his wife of more than 30 years, Hannah Storm, and their three daughters, Hannah, Ellery and Riley.

Rest in Peace, Dan Hicks.

Sources: NBC Sports; USA Today; PGA Tour; USGA; Golf Channel.
